name: MonarchTypingIndicator
title: TypingIndicator
summary: "Ana is typing…" under a conversation, with three bouncing dots, worded for one, two or several people.
whenToUse: Under a conversation, fed by the product's realtime layer with the names of the people typing now.
whenNotToUse: Not as a general loading indicator; use the standard ProgressView for that.
api: init(_ names: [String], text: String? = nil, reservesSpace: Bool = true, announcesChanges: Bool = true)

options.name: names
options.description: The display names of the people typing now, newest last, without the current user.

options.name: text
options.description: Replaces the built-in sentence. Shown only while somebody is typing.

options.name: reservesSpace
options.description: The line keeps its height while nobody is typing, so the conversation does not jump.

options.name: announcesChanges
options.description: A new sentence is announced to VoiceOver.

states.name: nobody
states.description: Nothing is drawn. With reservesSpace the height of one line is kept.

appearance: Dots in the subtle text colour and the sentence in the muted text colour, in the caption type role, in every theme.
platformNotes: Same wording rules as the web. The web takes people with an id and a messages object with three functions; iOS takes names and one text override, because the product can word the whole sentence itself. Announcements use an accessibility announcement instead of a live region.
accessibility: The dots are decorative; the sentence is one element.
A new sentence is announced once without moving focus, unless announcesChanges is false.
While nobody is typing the element is hidden from VoiceOver.
The dots stand still when Reduce Motion is on.
The text and the dots scale with Dynamic Type.
edgeCases: Names that are empty or white space are left out.
The built-in sentences are English; pass text for other languages and plural rules.
With reservesSpace false and nobody typing the view has no height.

examples.title: One, two and several people
